Consult Summary:
- Middle-aged male with 1-week history of atraumatic left elbow swelling, mildly warm and fluctuant, without pain or restricted movement.
- Video exam consistent with likely olecranon bursitis; septic arthritis unlikely. Plan includes NSAIDs, blood tests (inflammatory/infectious/rheumatologic/gout), and follow-up with safety-net advice.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Left elbow swelling (likely olecranon bursitis)
  - Timeline: Noted ~1 week ago; first episode. No preceding trauma or overuse.
  - Symptoms: Visible swelling with mild warmth; feels fluid; no significant pain; full range of motion preserved.
  - Pertinent negatives: No systemic illness reported; no prior similar episodes.
  - Family history: Denies known rheumatoid arthritis/lupus in family; uncertain overall.
  - Social/occupational: Desk-based job; not physically demanding.
  - Examination (video): Swelling over left olecranon region; tip skin appears dry; area warmer than adjacent skin; non-tender at olecranon tip with mild tenderness adjacent to swelling; movement intact; no features suggesting septic arthritis per clinician.
  - Differential: Olecranon bursitis most likely. Consider gout, inflammatory/rheumatologic causes, infection.
  - Plan: Start ibuprofen; order blood tests (inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, gout workup); follow-up after results; urgent care if redness/intense pain/spreading erythema develops.

Issue 2:
- Osteoarthritis (history)
  - Diagnosed by GP a few years ago.
  - Intermittent joint pains reported.
  - No current regular medications for this condition.

Issue 3:
- Peanut allergy
  - Reports allergy to peanuts.
  - No known medication allergies.

Medications:
- No regular medications reported.
- Ibuprofen 400 mg orally twice daily recommended (over-the-counter); take with food; stop if heartburn occurs.

Allergies:
- Peanuts.
- No known medication allergies.

Past Medical History:
- Osteoarthritis (diagnosed by GP a few years ago).

Social History:
- Desk job.
- Runs 2–3 times per week; active.
- Smoking status not documented.
- Alcohol intake not documented.

Preventative History:
- Not documented (cervical/prostate/colorectal screening, BMD, vaccinations, optometry/skin check not discussed).

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Video examination of left elbow: Visible swelling over olecranon area; skin at tip appears dry; warmer than surrounding skin; non-tender at tip with mild adjacent tenderness; full movement preserved; clinician states presentation not consistent with septic arthritis at this time.

Plan:
- Send blood test forms to patient.
  - Tests: Inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, gout evaluation.
- Start ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily with food; stop if heartburn occurs.
- Follow-up: Arrange clinic or telehealth review after blood tests are completed; results expected ~5–6 days after sampling.
- Safety-net: Seek urgent medical attention if elbow becomes very red, very painful, or if redness spreads/worsens.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vital signs; full medication reconciliation; smoking status; alcohol intake; vaccination and preventive screening history.
- Internal conflicts: Age stated as 53 vs. date of birth given as April 5, 1973 (conflict noted). Family history of rheumatologic disease both “denied” and “unsure” (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Occasional inaudible/unclear segments; overall adequate to determine assessment and plan.
